## Natural history notes

A medium-sized owlet moth characterized by mottled gray to brown forewings, dark wavy crosslines, and a bark-like pattern that helps it blend against tree trunks and dead leaves. In Florida, the Laugher Moth is found in hardwood forests, hammocks, mixed woods, forest edges, parks, and wooded yards where host trees such as oaks and other hardwoods occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on tree foliage and help transfer hardwood leaf growth into the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
